methodology.value: The Eliashberg equation is used to predict superconductivity. The supplied text does not explicitly identify its isotropic or anisotropic variant.

key_findings.value: Calibrated readings of Fig. 4 give ScH6 Tc values of approximately 100 K for μ*=0.1 and 86 K for μ*=0.13 at 300 GPa. Graph-reading resolution is not physical measurement uncertainty.

coverage_exclusions.reason: Reports structural, packing and energetic results primarily for other hydrides, not ScH6 superconductivity records.

FIG. 4.
Calculated electronic DOS of H at the Fermi level (NEf)
per Å3 (top panel), the EPC parameter λ (middle panel), and Tc
(bottom panel) of various clathrate structures at high pressures.
The pressure values chosen within their stable pressure ranges of
the phases are 300, 400, 120, 150, 400, 100, 50, 100, 200, and
100 GPa for ScH6, ScH9, YH6, YH9, YH10, LaH6, LaH9, CeH9,
CeH10, and PrH9, respectively.

point (Fig. S14 [38]), the large λ values are mainly associated
with in-plane stretching, in-plane rocking, and out-of-plane
rocking vibrations of H clathrate cages (Fig. S15 [38]).
The Eliashberg equation [37] gives a better description of
systems with strong electron-phonon coupling for λ > 1.5.
We have therefore used the Eliashberg equation to predict
superconductivity in the clathrate structures using the
calculated logarithmic average frequency (ωlog) and typical
Coulomb pseudopotential parameters (μ) from 0.1 to 0.13.
The resulting Tc values are 276 K (253 K for μ ¼ 0.13)
and 303 K (287 K for μ ¼ 0.13) using μ ¼ 0.1 for YH9 at
150 GPa and YH10 at 400 GPa, respectively. The calculated
Tc of LaH10 reaches 288 K using μ ¼ 0.1 at 200 GPa. We
also investigated potential superconductivity in other clath-
rate structures (Fig. 4) and predicted Tc values for ScH6 and
ScH9 as high as ∼150 K, although for LaH9, CeH9, CeH10,
and PrH9 they are much lower at <56 K (Fig. 4) due to the
introduction of much heavier elements which reduce BCS
superconductivity.

The H clathrate structures of REH6, REH9, and REH10
are metallic as seen from the calculated electronic band
structures and densities of states (Figs. S13 and S14 [38]).
The electronic density of states at the Fermi level is
typically large and is dominated by the contribution from
H atoms. To examine potential superconductivity in the
clathrate structures, lattice phonons and electron-phonon
coupling (EPC) calculations were carried out using linear
response theory [68]. Encouragingly, the resulting EPC
parameters, λ, of YH9 and YH10 are quite large and reach
values of 4.42 and 2.41 at 150 and 400 GPa, respectively.
Besides the H-derived high density of states at the Fermi
level that is associated with a van Hove singularity at the Γ
